sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `gemini-cli`
- Canonical name: Gemini CLI (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-identity`)
- Current status: consumer Gemini CLI access ended 2026-06-18; Google sent consumers to Antigravity CLI. Enterprise Code Assist Standard/Enterprise and paid API keys remain. Official quota docs still listed consumer plans at the 2026-08-10 check (`claim-gemini-cli-sf-consumer-ended-2026-08-15`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-status-transition`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-status-docs`).
- Homepage leftover copy: on 2026-08-16 geminicli.com still banners unpaid/Google One replacement by Antigravity CLI on June 18th, future tense (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-homepage-future-tense-banner`). Banner is not proof the consumer path is still live.
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-15

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: an open-source, terminal-first Google agent runtime (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-identity`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-primary-type`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-unique`).
- What it is not: checked sources do not establish a native mobile app, mobile web app, messaging gateway, vendor relay, or provider-neutral local-primary-model runtime (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-not-for`).

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-primary-type`)
- Agent-loop owner: `@google/gemini-cli-core` owns chat, scheduling, tool calls, history, and compression (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-loop-owner`).
- Architecture: local Node process and local tools, with model calls sent to selected Google services (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-execution`).

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-gemini-cli-interactive`, `surface-gemini-cli-headless`, `surface-gemini-cli-vscode`, `surface-gemini-cli-acp-ide`, `surface-gemini-cli-cloud-shell`, `surface-gemini-cli-cloud-workstations`, `surface-gemini-cli-sdk`, `surface-gemini-cli-a2a-server`.
- Execution location: same-device runtime by default; Cloud Shell and Cloud Workstations are host environments; the experimental A2A package is operator-hosted if deployed (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-execution`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-surface-cloud-hosts`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-surface-a2a`).

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: Google service paths provide Gemini models; stable and nightly versions remain distinct (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-provider-auth`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-version-conflict`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-version-main`).
- Auth strategy: Google sign-in, Gemini API key, and Vertex AI credentials or keys (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-provider-auth`).
- Provider support: Google Code Assist, Gemini Developer API, and Vertex AI. General third-party provider or custom-base-URL support remains unknown (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-provider-auth`).

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: hierarchical GEMINI.md context is separate from local session persistence (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-context-hierarchy`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-context-session`).
- Memory: repository, private-project, and global Markdown memory files can carry facts into later sessions (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-memory-files`).
- Compaction: automatic and manual history compression (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-compaction`).
- Session behavior: local save, resume, and checkpoint branching (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-context-session`).

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: mutating tools require manual confirmation; approval modes and policy decisions are documented separately (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-security`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-policy`).
- Extensions: prompts, MCP servers, commands, themes, hooks, subagents, skills, and policy files (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-extension-stack`).
- MCP: packaged and configured through extensions; explicit environment and token boundaries remain operator-managed (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-extension-stack`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-mcp-security`).
- Skills: supported in extensions (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-extension-stack`).
- Hooks: supported in extensions and execute with user privileges (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-extension-stack`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-hook-security`).
- APIs: in-process SDK and experimental A2A server (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-surface-sdk`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-surface-a2a`).

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: preview local subagents and remote A2A subagents (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-orchestration`).
- Parallelism: the scheduler can run parallelizable tool-call batches while forcing selected calls to stay sequential; durable parallel-agent workflows remain unestablished (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-parallelism`).

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: optional Docker, Podman, Seatbelt, Windows native sandboxing, gVisor, and experimental LXC are documented, while default wording conflicts across official pages (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-sandbox`).
- Permissions: mutating tools require manual confirmation, while approval modes and allow/deny/ask-user rules come from the policy engine (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-security`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-policy`).
- Security: manual confirmation for mutating tools and policy-engine modes and rules are separate from Trusted Folders, user-privileged hooks, and explicit MCP environment/token handling (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-security`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-policy`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-trusted-folders`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-hook-security`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-mcp-security`).
- Data path: sessions and memory stay local; model requests use Google services; optional telemetry and MCP paths remain separate (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-data-path`).

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
- Interface and surface IDs:
  - Terminal: `surface-gemini-cli-interactive`, `surface-gemini-cli-headless` (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-surface-cli`).
  - IDE: `surface-gemini-cli-vscode`, `surface-gemini-cli-acp-ide` (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-surface-ide`).
  - Hosted terminal environments: `surface-gemini-cli-cloud-shell`, `surface-gemini-cli-cloud-workstations` (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-surface-cloud-hosts`).
  - Programmatic: `surface-gemini-cli-sdk`, `surface-gemini-cli-a2a-server` (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-surface-sdk`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-surface-a2a`).
- Remote behavior: no first-party remote client or vendor relay was established. The A2A package is experimental and not treated as a Google-hosted service (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-not-for`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-surface-a2a`).
- Mobile behavior: native mobile, mobile web, messaging, and Termux-specific product support remain unknown (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-not-for`).
- Background behavior: durable hosted jobs, scheduling, and resumable remote work remain unknown; headless CLI and background shell processes do not establish them (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-not-for`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-surface-cli`).

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: current docs advertise consumer plans and quotas, but the consumer transition announcement creates an unresolved availability conflict (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-status-transition`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-status-docs`).
- License: Apache-2.0 source and packages (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-license`).
- Maintenance: v0.54.4 stable and 0.56.0 nightly are separate observations (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-version-conflict`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-version-main`).
- Lock-in: source is open, but documented model and auth paths depend on Google services (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-provider-auth`, `claim-gemini-cli-w2-drawback`).

sections.heading: Lineage and compatibility edges
sections.body:
- Lineage claims: no first-party lineage statement beyond repository metadata was established.
- Relationship edges: no new outgoing Gemini CLI row. New inbound Wave 2 rows are `goose --connects_via--> gemini-cli` and `goose --reuses_auth_from--> gemini-cli`, both for the deprecated pass-through route.

sections.heading: Closest substitutes, partial substitutes, same-lineage relatives, often-confused products, and complements
sections.body:
- Comparison neighborhood IDs: `unknown`; no new Wave 2 neighborhood row was emitted.
- Substitutes: `unknown`
- Partial substitutes: `unknown`
- Same-lineage relatives: `unknown`
- Often-confused products: Antigravity CLI is named by the transition notice but was outside the six-product research scope; no record was emitted.
- Complements: Goose has a deprecated Gemini CLI compatibility path, but no neighborhood membership was asserted.

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: terminal-first access to Google's Gemini agent and service paths (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-unique`).
- Meaningful drawbacks: Google service dependence, internet needs, transition uncertainty, optional sandbox setup, and hook/MCP trust (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-drawback`).
- Best fit: `unknown`
- Not-for: unverified native-mobile, messaging, relay, hosted-durable, and provider-neutral local-model needs (`claim-gemini-cli-w2-not-for`).
